verdict: REJECT — would not pass plan check. 7 FAIL (P1 P2 P3 P4, C2 C3 C5), 5 FLAG (C1 C4 C6, A2 A3), 1 PASS (A1). The underlying data is sound — scale bars are accurate to <0.1% on every sheet, every legend circuit is drawn, device counts reconcile with the takeoff exactly (demo 69, gabled 25) — but the sheet compositor fails drafting basics. Every sheet auto-fits its own scale and origin (demo prints at five different scales: 58.51/43.48/52.63/42.94/43.75 px/m), so foundation walls never register under framing under electrical; the gabled foundation perimeter has a ~1 m open gap where the p_link connector wall has no footing at all (a framed load-bearing wall bearing on nothing — automatic rejection); oblique corners are square-cut butt joints with 0.2–0.4 m overshoots, wedge gaps and rebar tails poking into space; anchor bolts are double-plotted (76 drawn vs 31 scheduled, 88 vs 36); no device symbol (R/G/S/L/SD/P, SO/SR/CO/WH/AH/RA/T/EF) is defined in any legend and both foundation sheets have no legend at all; demo sheet 7 ships ~95% blank while the engine's three model warnings (duplicate walls skipped, Living/Kitchen has no floor slab, slab-on-grade) never print anywhere. Product-owner flags adjudicated: 'missing electrical circuits' REFUTED (all 11 FL / 7 NY circuits drawn, zero missing devices); 'misalignment' CONFIRMED (P2); 'weird-shaped concrete bases' CONFIRMED (P3); 'incompleteness' CONFIRMED (P1/C1/C3/C5).

P1.note: CONFIRMED. Demo sheet 7 is ~95% blank white: only the 'Material takeoff — sheet 2 of 2' title, three red RO-shift flag lines (54.5cm / 89.5cm / 3.3cm) bottom-left, and the title block. Demo framing and roof sheets auto-fit the drawing into the right two-thirds of the frame (~35–38% coverage) leaving the whole lower-left quadrant dead except a small legend; the gabled schedules sheet is ~30–35% empty below its two text columns. Content is never centered in the free field between legend and title block. Sheet 6's bottom fifth is empty, so the three flags fit there — sheet 7 has no reason to exist.
P1.recommendation: Kill sheet 7: flow the flags list onto sheet 6 and paginate schedules only when column content exceeds ~70% of a sheet. Center each drawing in the frame after subtracting legend/title reserves, and enforce a max-30%-empty check in the sheet compositor.

P2.evidence: demo-house-FL sheets 1–5; gabled-composite-NY sheets 1–4 (all plan sheets, both sets)
P2.note: CONFIRMS the owner's 'misalignment' flag. Every sheet auto-fits its own scale AND origin: demo prints at five scales in one set — 58.51 (foundation), 43.48 (framing), 52.63 (roof), 42.94 (electrical), 43.75 (plumbing) px/m; foundation is ~35% larger than framing, and even electrical vs plumbing (identical footprint) drift 1.9% — close enough to look aligned, wrong enough to fail any overlay. Gabled: 61.27 vs 49.40–49.74 px/m. Origins shift too (demo north wall at sheet-y ~74 px on foundation vs ~150 px on framing; foundation drawn far left, framing shoved right; scale bars of identical drawn length labeled '3 m' vs '4 m'). The roof sheet draws the 12.4x7.9 m roof segment as a bare rectangle with no building outline beneath, impossible to locate over the composite footprint. A light-table / PDF-layer check — the first thing a plans examiner does — is impossible. Scale bars are present so each sheet is individually usable.
P2.recommendation: Compute one shared bounding box (union of all systems on the level, incl. roof overhang) and one transform per plan set; snap it to a standard ratio (1:50 / 1:100) and reuse it on every plan sheet (schedules exempt). Keep legend/title outside the fit box so they cannot perturb the scale; print the ratio next to the bar; ghost a light building-outline underlay on roof, electrical and plumbing sheets.

P3.note: CONFIRMS the owner's 'weird-shaped concrete bases'. All oblique foundation corners are square-cut butt joints (measured in the SVG at 61.27 px/m): west corner — diagonal stemwall lines overshoot 0.19–0.38 m past the wall face into open air as a visible spur; apex — the centre stemwall pokes exactly 0.31 m through the gable point while both diagonal runs stop 0.19–0.32 m short, leaving wedge gaps; NE/SE corners — wall lines overshoot 0.14–0.27 m past the crossing runs (T-overshoots). Rebar polylines protrude beyond the concrete into empty space at the NW corner; the slab halo is drawn per-run as squared-end rectangles, producing wedge slivers at every oblique corner. The framing sheet's NE corner leaves a detached plate sliver plus an open gap. Demo: a stale 8x5 m wall rectangle is rendered as real footing+stemwall and its runs cross the room-block footings in full X junctions at (4,0) and (0,2.5) with no junction treatment — even though the panel itself warns those walls are duplicates. Demo orthogonal corners butt acceptably; line-weight hierarchy (structure/context/annotation) is fine.
P3.recommendation: Miter footing/stemwall polygons at the corner bisector for every non-orthogonal join (intersect the offset polylines instead of butt-capping strokes); clip stemwall/rebar lines to the mitered concrete outline; union all slab halos into one closed polygon; snap run endpoints to shared corner vertices; dedupe walls the engine already flags as duplicates before drawing; add a corner-closure assertion (endpoint coincidence < 1 cm) in the plan-set builder.

P4.evidence: both electrical sheets; both plumbing+HVAC sheets; both foundation sheets; demo-house-FL/6-schedules-takeoff-1-2.png; gabled-composite-NY/5-schedules-takeoff.png
P4.note: Device tag symbols are used everywhere but defined nowhere: R, G, S, L, SD, P on both electrical sheets (legends list only circuit IDs) and SO, SR, CO, WH, AH, RA, T, EF on both plumbing+HVAC sheets (legends list only 3 pipe/duct line types). Both foundation sheets have NO legend at all — rebar double-lines, anchor-bolt squares and two gray tones (footing halo vs stemwall) are unexplained. Takeoff rows are ellipsized mid-word (~26 rows on demo sheet 6, ~20 on gabled sheet 5: 'NEC 210.8 wet locatio…', '(field splice — run …', 'R403.1…', '1440 V…') with ample blank space below for wrapping. Symbol bubbles collide: SO/SR and SR/EF on demo plumbing, L/SD on gabled electrical, plus AH/SR, SR/EF and SO/CO/SO pileups on gabled plumbing. No room labels anywhere, so circuit zones (bathroom, kitchen) cannot be verified against rooms. Text sizes themselves pass (min 8px).
P4.recommendation: Add a symbol legend block to every sheet that uses symbols (device tags on electrical/plumbing; rebar/bolt/gray-tone rows on foundation); wrap takeoff rows to a second line instead of truncating; nudge coincident device bubbles apart along the wall with short leaders; print room names on plan sheets.

C1.note: PARTLY CONFIRMS 'incompleteness'. Every system with members gets a sheet in both sets — gabled has zero roof member nodes, so its missing roof sheet is defensible, and the drawings are faithful to the model. But the demo roof sheet shows a single rafter rectangle 13.34x8.84 m (main body 12x7.5 + walls + 0.45 m eaves) only; the 8x5 m wing at (-4,-2.5)–(4,2.5) has no roof structure on any sheet and isn't even outlined as context — the set silently reads as a house with an unroofed habitable wing. The manifest's warnings ('Living/Kitchen has no floor slab', duplicate walls skipped, slab-on-grade) appear on zero sheets; a 'gabled' set ships with no roof drawing, also silently. Silently partial coverage is what an examiner rejects.
C1.recommendation: Emit visible flags (like the RO-shift flags) when a level's footprint area has no members of a system — 'wing (-4,-2.5)-(4,2.5) has no roof members' / 'no roof system in model' — on the schedules sheet and in the plan-set JSON verdict; surface engine warnings on the affected sheet; draw the uncovered footprint dashed on the roof plan.

C2.note: Owner's 'missing electrical circuits' REFUTED at the data level: all 11 (FL) and 7 (NY) legend circuits have drawn colored runs (verified per stroke color in the SVGs — e.g. GEN-2 #d145d3 x39, BA-1 #296bae x26), legend rows carry breaker/gauge/zone, homeruns lead back to panel P, and device totals equal the takeoff exactly (70 bubbles = 69 devices + panel; 26 = 25 + panel). The 'missing' impression comes from congested same-wall homerun bundles at print size. BUT the sheet still fails traceability: orphan duplicate device symbols float off-wall with NO wiring (demo: R at SVG ~(1675,585), S+R mid-room at ~(1410,1015/1055); gabled: R below the notch at ~(1218,1143)) — devices without visible wiring = incomplete per the checklist; a dead-end wire stub protrudes at the gabled notch; the four GEN circuit colors are near-identical magentas (RGB deltas confined to one channel) indistinguishable at 1–1.5px strokes; multiple circuits stack on the same wall path with zero circuit-ID labels on any run, so individual circuits cannot be traced panel-to-device; and R/G/S/L/SD/P are never defined in a legend.
C2.recommendation: Remove or wire the duplicate device symbols; label each run with its circuit ID at intervals; fan out parallel homeruns with a 1–2 px offset per circuit; re-pick circuit colors for contrast (or add per-run text tags); add a device-symbol legend block (R receptacle, G GFCI, S switch, L luminaire, SD smoke alarm, P panel).

C3.note: CONFIRMED. Gabled perimeter footing is NOT continuous: the 1 m p_link connector wall (7,10)->(7,11) has essentially no footing/stemwall — the SVG has 14 stemwall lines for 8 walls and the bottom step shows a ~1 m open white gap between the left building's bottom run and the lower right-building run (footing band and stemwall strokes just stop in space). A load-bearing framed wall bearing on nothing is an automatic plan-check rejection (the framing sheet frames that same wall). Oblique corners additionally gap/overshoot ~0.2–0.3 m (see P3). Demo: runs are continuous and interior footings present (that part passes), but footings cross in X junctions at the stale-wing overlap; anchor bolts exist only on the main-body rectangle — the entire 8x5 m wing perimeter has zero bolt marks; every bolt is double-plotted (drawn marks pair into near-coincident duplicates: 76 = 38 pairs vs takeoff 31; 88 = 44 pairs vs 36 — a residual count gap remains even deduped), with irrational 0.10 m bolt pairs on the gabled 7 m south wall; and neither sheet has any anchor-bolt count/spacing callout.
C3.recommendation: Trace the wall graph, not per-wall strokes, so p_link gets its footing and every foundation path Z-closes; assert at build time that each foundation run set forms closed rings (or explicitly tagged openings) before the sheet is emitted; miter all corners; plot exactly one bolt series per run reconciled to the takeoff count; extend bolts to all exterior stemwalls; add a text callout ('1/2" AB @ 6'-0" O.C. — 31 PCS PER R403.1.6') that matches the takeoff.

C4.note: Openings read correctly at zoom — orange header blocks with doubled trimmer/king ticks on both sets, and the legend gives member sizes. But there is no stud-spacing callout anywhere (complete text inventory of both framing sheets contains no 'o.c.' string); headers/beams carry no size tags at the openings themselves (4x8 FL / 4x10 NY inferable only from the legend); the roof plan has no rafter-spacing note; and the gabled NE plate corner is open with a detached sliver, with stub overshoots and gaps where oblique walls meet vertical at the apex and right eave.
C4.recommendation: Add 'STUDS @ 16" O.C. TYP.' and 'RAFTERS @ 24" O.C.' (or actual spacing) as general notes; tag each header with its per-sheet size ('4x8 HDR' FL, '4x10 HDR' NY) at the opening; label any girder/beam runs; clean the oblique plate corner joins (same miter/snap pass as P3).

C5.note: The takeoff is internally consistent and device counts reconcile exactly — demo: 28 receptacles + 25 GFCI + 7 switches + 6 lights + 3 smoke alarms = 69 = sum of the 11 per-circuit rows = devices drawn; gabled 25 = 7+13+1+3+1 = sum of 7 circuit rows; gabled studs 90 drawn = 90 in takeoff — keep all that. But: (1) drawn anchor-bolt marks contradict the schedule (76 drawn vs '31 pcs'; 88 vs '36 pcs' — double-plotted series, and 38/44 even after dedup); (2) ~20–26 rows per takeoff sheet are ellipsized mid-word so quantity basis notes cannot be audited; (3) the flags list is NOT intact: demo prints only the three RO-shift flags while the build's three engine warnings (6 duplicate overlapping walls skipped; Living/Kitchen has no floor slab; slab-on-grade) appear nowhere, and the gabled sheet has no flags block at all despite its slab-on-grade warning in the manifest. The set hides known model problems an examiner should see.
C5.recommendation: Wrap all takeoff lines to a second row; print the complete warnings list verbatim (engine warnings + RO shifts) in the flags block on both sets; make the drawn anchor-bolt symbol count the same number the takeoff reports; add an automated drawn-symbols-vs-takeoff-rows reconciliation test to the export pipeline.

C6.note: Title blocks carry project, level, jurisdiction + full code name with effective date (FL: 'Florida Building Code, Residential — 8th Edition (2023), 2021 IRC base, effective 2023-12-31'; NY: '2025 Residential Code of New York State (2024 IRC base), effective 2025-12-31'), LOD, date and disclaimer on every sheet — good. Missing: set-wide sheet numbering — 'Sheet n/N' appears nowhere (the foundation sheet is not '1/7'; only the FL schedules pair reads '(1/2)'/'(2/2)'; the NY schedules sheet has no number at all); no stated scale ratio in the block; no sheet index. The code citation wraps mid-parenthetical on every NY sheet ('…New York State (2024 | IRC base), effective…') and splits '8th | Edition (2023)' on all 7 FL sheets.
C6.recommendation: Add 'SHEET n/N' plus the sheet's scale ratio to every title block using the set's sheet index; add a sheet index on sheet 1; reflow the code line at word boundaries so parentheticals don't break.

A1.note: Scale bars are internally accurate on every sheet, worst error <0.1% (spot checks within ~2% once footing projections are allowed) — far inside the 5% gate. Demo: the 12.00 m main body measures 58.50 u/m vs the 3 m bar's 58.51 (<0.1%); the 8.000 m graph wall measures 0.003% off the framing bar; roof deck = 13.30 m = 12.4 m segment + 2x0.45 m overhang at 52.63 px/m. Gabled: the 7.00 m north wall and 9 m spine / 8 m east wall measure exactly per the bars on foundation, framing, electrical and plumbing sheets. (The short-drawn oblique runs are P3 endpoint-placement errors, not scale errors; each sheet picking a different non-standard scale is flagged under P2.)
A1.recommendation: Keep the bar generation; snap the chosen scale to standard ratios and print the named ratio ('1:50') beside the bar once P2's locked scale lands.

A2.evidence: demo-house-FL/2-wall-framing-plan.png vs 6-schedules-takeoff-1-2.png; gabled-composite-NY/2-wall-framing-plan.png vs 5-schedules-takeoff.png; both foundation sheets
A2.note: Gabled is an exact PASS: 90 drawn 2x4 stud symbols = takeoff '2x4 — 90 pcs (8 ft stock)'; the east 8 m wall shows field studs at 0.406 m = true 16 in o.c. with king/trimmer pairs at openings, obliques also at 16 in o.c. Demo wood walls are consistent (~21 stud ticks over the 8 m wing top wall ≈ 16" o.c., 3-stud corner packs) and electrical devices match the takeoff exactly on both sets (69 and 25). BUT the demo CMU walls are uncountable: 715 full-size block rects drawn where a one-course plan view needs ~150 — the 12 m y=7.5 run alone has 247 block symbols of which 200 are byte-identical duplicate SVG elements stacked up to 6 deep — and the legend lists only wood members, no CMU symbol at all despite '1015 pcs 8x8x16 running bond' in the takeoff. Anchor bolts: 76 (demo) / 88 (gabled) drawn vs takeoff 31 / 36 pcs (~2.4x, double-plotted; recorded as FAIL under C3/C5).
A2.recommendation: Dedupe members before rendering (no two identical rects); draw exactly one CMU course in plan with a 'CMU 8x8x16 running bond' legend row; add 16/24 in o.c. spacing callouts per wall; print per-run anchor-bolt count/spacing notes that reconcile with the takeoff number.

A3.note: Plan orientation is consistent — coordinate mapping of anchor walls proves one y-down/north-up transform on every sheet of both sets (demo y=-2.5 wall always at top, gabled ridge always top-centre). But not a single sheet of the 12 carries a north arrow, datum mark, origin cross or grid line (grep of all SVGs and plan-set.html: zero hits for north/compass/datum) — orientation is only verifiable by comparing wall shapes, and combined with P2's per-sheet auto-fit there is no visual anchor an examiner can register against. The roof framing sheet draws only the bare rafter rectangle with zero wall context, so its registration to the floor plan cannot be confirmed visually (the plumbing sheet already ghosts a wall outline, proving the precedent exists in-set).
A3.recommendation: Stamp a north arrow next to the scale bar and a shared origin/datum cross at the same world coordinate on every plan sheet; ghost the wall outline (light grey, as the plumbing sheet does) under the roof framing so rafter bearing lines can be checked against walls.

recommendations: Lock ONE scale and ONE origin per plan set (P2/A3): compute the union bounding box of all systems on the level (incl. roof overhang), snap the fit to a standard ratio (1:50 or 1:100), and reuse that single transform on every plan sheet; reserve legend/title-block areas OUTSIDE the fit box so they cannot perturb the scale; print the ratio next to the scale bar.

Build foundation runs from the wall graph, not per-wall strokes (C3/P3): trace closed rings so the 1 m p_link connector gets its footing; miter footing/stemwall polygons at the corner bisector by intersecting the offset polylines (no butt-capped strokes); clip stemwall/rebar lines to the mitered concrete outline; union slab halos into one closed polygon; assert endpoint coincidence < 1 cm and ring closure before emitting the sheet.

Dedupe members before rendering (A2/C3/C5): drop byte-identical SVG rects (200 duplicate CMU blocks on one run, every anchor bolt double-plotted); draw exactly one CMU course in plan; plot one bolt series per run reconciled to the takeoff count, extend bolts to every exterior stemwall, and print a '1/2" AB @ 6'-0" O.C. — N PCS' callout that equals the takeoff number.

Add symbol legends everywhere symbols are used (P4/C2): device blocks R/G/S/L/SD/P on electrical and SO/SR/CO/WH/AH/RA/T/EF on plumbing+HVAC; a foundation legend for rebar double-lines, anchor-bolt squares and the two gray tones; and remove-or-wire the floating duplicate device symbols, label each wire run with its circuit ID at intervals, offset parallel homeruns 1–2 px per circuit, and re-pick the four near-identical GEN magentas.

Fix schedules pagination and truncation (P1/C5): drop sheet 7 by flowing the flags block onto sheet 6 and only paginating when content exceeds ~70% of a sheet; wrap takeoff rows to a second line instead of ellipsizing; print the complete engine warnings (duplicate walls skipped, 'Living/Kitchen has no floor slab', slab-on-grade) verbatim in the flags block on both sets.

Center drawings and enforce sheet balance (P1): after subtracting legend/title reserves, center the drawing in the remaining frame and add a max-30%-empty compositor check; surface a visible flag when a footprint area has no members of a system ('wing has no roof members') and draw the uncovered footprint dashed on the roof plan (C1).

Add registration furniture to every plan sheet (A3): a north arrow beside the scale bar and a shared origin/datum cross at the same world coordinate across the set; ghost the wall outline (light grey, as the plumbing sheet already does) under the roof framing and electrical sheets.

Complete the title block and annotations (C6/C4): 'SHEET n/N' plus the scale ratio on every title block, a sheet index on sheet 1, word-boundary wrapping for the code citation; add 'STUDS @ 16" O.C. TYP.' / 'RAFTERS @ 24" O.C.' general notes and per-sheet header size tags ('4x8 HDR' FL, '4x10 HDR' NY) at each opening.
